findings.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — P1 confidence 100: `return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))` applies a numeric cursor codec to the endpoint's `order_by="-datetime"`, so generating a cursor for any nonempty audit-log page raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime` instead of returning that page.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — P1 confidence 100: `use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"` replaces the former date-range filtering block without a replacement, so existing requests supplying `start`/`end` or `statsPeriod` silently return audit events outside the requested interval on both pagination paths, breaking the existing request contract.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:845 — Advisory P2 confidence 75: `def get_result(self, limit=100, cursor=None, count_hits=False, known_hits=None, max_hits=None):` duplicates the base paginator's query, count, reverse-page correction, cursor-building, and post-filter algorithm, so the next boundary-condition fix in BasePaginator leaves optimized administrators on the stale implementation unless maintainers update both copies; the strongest rebuttal is that advanced offset selection needs separate behavior, but extracting that single selection operation makes this entire duplicated get_result override unnecessary while retaining the policy difference.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:882 — P1 confidence 100: `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` passes a negative start directly to Django whenever advanced features are enabled and `cursor.offset < 0`, so the advertised negative-offset pagination cannot execute because Django rejects negative QuerySet indexing before issuing SQL ([Django dependency contract](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/5.1/topics/db/queries/#limiting-querysets)).

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — P1 confidence 100: `return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))` raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime` when the optimized audit-log request returns its first row because `order_by="-datetime"` supplies a datetime to the numeric key converter, aborting cursor construction and returning a 500 instead of the audit-log page.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:882 — P2 confidence 100: `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` passes the negative offset accepted by the new advanced branch directly into Django QuerySet slicing, so an authorized request with `optimized_pagination=true&cursor=0:-1:0` raises an uncaught negative-indexing exception and returns a 500 instead of rejecting the cursor or serving the promised reverse page.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:68 — [P1, confidence 100] Removing `queryset = queryset.filter(datetime__range=(start, end))` expands the pagination-performance change into removal of existing date filtering, so audit-log callers supplying `start`/`end` or `statsPeriod` receive entries outside the requested interval even without opting into optimized pagination.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates nearly the entire get_result() method from BasePaginator (lines 845-912 in the new code). Looking at the diff, the only meaningful difference is the negative offset handling in lines 878-885. This is a valid maintainability concern - if BasePaginator's get_result() is updated with bug fixes, OptimizedCursorPaginator won't receive those fixes automatically. The suggestion to extract just the offset selection logic rather than duplicating the entire method is architecturally sound. This is a real, specific concern grounded in the diff, not a bug but an important design/maintenance issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — P1 confidence 100: `return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))` raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime` when the optimized audit-log request returns its first row because `order_by="-datetime"` supplies a datetime to the numeric key converter, aborting cursor construction and returning a 500 instead of the audit-log page.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key() at line 840 calls `int(math.floor(value))` or `int(math.ceil(value))` on the value obtained from `getattr(item, self.key)`. When used with audit logs via `order_by="-datetime"`, the key would be 'datetime' and the value would be a datetime object. math.floor/math.ceil require real numbers, not datetime objects, so this would raise TypeError. The DateTimePaginator (the original paginator) handles datetime fields properly, but this new OptimizedCursorPaginator does not have datetime-specific handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:882 — P2 confidence 100: `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` passes the negative offset accepted by the new advanced branch directly into Django QuerySet slicing, so an authorized request with `optimized_pagination=true&cursor=0:-1:0` raises an uncaught negative-indexing exception and returns a 500 instead of rejecting the cursor or serving the promised reverse page.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result() at lines 879-883, when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0, the code sets start_offset = cursor.offset (a negative value) and then executes queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices and will raise an AssertionError or similar exception. The finding correctly identifies that this code path would cause a 500 error when an authorized user sends a request with a negative cursor offset like cursor=0:-1:0. The code comment claims 'Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' but this is incorrect - Django explicitly rejects negative indexing.

However, examining the diff carefully, there is no such line being removed. The diff shows changes to the pagination logic (lines 68-93) but the date filtering code that would appear earlier in the function (around lines 50-65 based on the context) is not shown as being modified or removed.
